_instructions: This is the single source of truth for your library. Edit, correct, or replace entries here — David should verify all of these. Fields: title, venue, date (YYYY-MM-DD, use YYYY-01-01 if only year known), type (op-ed | journal article | report | working paper | teaching case | chapter | white paper), url, coauthors (array, empty if solo), summary (2-3 sentences, especially important for paywalled pieces), topics (array of tags), paywalled (true/false), featured (true to pin in the 'New & Notable' spotlight).

publications.title: Digital public infrastructure and the economics of public value: what is 'public' about DPI?
publications.summary: Argues that digital public infrastructure should be created and governed to maximize public value, not merely regulated, and makes explicit the normative values embedded in how DPI is developed.

publications.title: Governments Can't Agree on What AI Actually Is
publications.summary: A core obstacle to international AI coordination is that governments hold fundamentally different beliefs about what AI is — imminent superintelligence versus a slower-moving sectoral technology. These divergent framings drive divergent national strategies and make agreement on governance elusive.

publications.title: Will AI Produce the Next Great Divergence?
publications.summary: Drawing on the 'critical junctures' framing from institutional economics, this essay argues AI could magnify small institutional differences between countries into a new global divergence, identifying four reasons AI is a uniquely powerful accelerator of institutional change.

publications.title: Teaching Public Service in the Digital Age: Collectively Building a Global Curriculum
publications.summary: Documents the participatory action research behind the Teaching Public Service in the Digital Age project, deriving eight digital-era competencies and open teaching tools for public administration educators.

publications.title: The Path to a Sovereign Tech Stack is Via a Commodified Tech Stack
publications.summary: Countries pursuing expensive, incompatible 'sovereign' tech stacks risk building gilded cages. Strategic standardization and commodification of cloud infrastructure, backed by procurement power, is the more effective route to digital sovereignty.

publications.title: 2025 State of Digital Public Infrastructure Report
publications.venue: UCL Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose
publications.summary: Built on the DPI Map, this report provides a global snapshot of digital ID, payments, and data-exchange systems across 210 countries, and analyzes how DPI is moving from experiment to scale.

publications.title: A Bottom-Up Approach to Building a Climate Resilience Stack
publications.venue: UCL Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose
publications.summary: Proposes the digital technologies and shared infrastructure — a 'climate resilience stack' — that could underpin climate monitoring and adaptation, built bottom-up from existing deployments. Prepared for COP30.

publications.title: The Service Gap: Europe's International Digital Strategy 2025
publications.summary: Responds to the EU's International Digital Strategy, arguing Europe's competitiveness and 'reliable partner' ambitions are undermined by a gap in actual digital service delivery capability.

publications.title: Learning From the Legacy of 18F
publications.summary: After the shutdown of 18F in March 2025, examines the unit's origins, what worked and what didn't, and lessons for future government digital service teams.

publications.title: The Economics of Shared Digital Infrastructures
publications.summary: Develops an economic framework for how governments should value, fund, and account for shared digital infrastructure. Has informed engagement with the World Bank, UK Treasury, and the G20 Digital Economy Working Group.

publications.title: How to Achieve Universal Access to Digital IDs
publications.summary: Proposes five guiding principles for designing reliable digital ID systems: minimizing data collection, engaging civil society, lowering costs through open-source ecosystems, strengthening global standards, and sustaining international support. With roughly 850 million people lacking legal identification, universal digital ID access by 2030 is within reach if systems are tailored to national contexts.

publications.title: AI's Efficiency Wars Have Begun
publications.summary: On DeepSeek-R1's release and how dramatically cheaper inference shifts the US–China AI race from raw capability toward efficiency competition, with implications for governments everywhere.

publications.title: Digital Public Infrastructure: a framework for conceptualisation and measurement
publications.summary: Uses a grounded-theory approach to define DPI's attributes across technology, public-interest values, and adoption context, plus the measurement framework underlying the DPI Map methodology.

publications.title: Unpacking Digital ID Systems' Early Policy Process: The Case of Jamaica's NIDS
publications.summary: Analyzes the early policy process behind Jamaica's National Identification System (NIDS), unpacking the political, legal, and administrative complexity of digital ID policy design. Conceptualizes four tensions that emerge during the process and draws lessons for more accountable, just, and inclusive ID system design. Open access.

publications.title: What Is Digital Public Infrastructure and Why Does It Matter?
publications.summary: Explains what distinguishes DPI from earlier e-government efforts: it digitizes critical societal functions like identity, payments, and data sharing rather than specific services, and combines an infrastructural role with public-interest governance. Draws on the DPI Map to show DPI is more widespread than assumed.

publications.title: An Agentic Shield? Using AI Agents to Enhance the Cybersecurity of Digital Public Infrastructure
publications.summary: Outlines how autonomous AI agents could strengthen the cybersecurity of digital public infrastructure, from detecting zero-day vulnerabilities and red-teaming to real-time defense. Cautions that agents are themselves vulnerable to attacks like prompt injection, and recommends governments pilot agents in low-risk use cases.

publications.title: Digital Public Infrastructure is the New Global Tech Bet — But Everyone's Betting on Something Different
publications.summary: Countries pursue DPI for divergent goals — financial inclusion, competition, economic integration. Uses Brazil's PIX and India's UPI to illustrate diverging outcomes and expectations.

publications.title: Interactions Between Artificial Intelligence and Digital Public Infrastructure: Concepts, Benefits, and Challenges
publications.summary: Explores how AI and digital public infrastructure can mutually enhance each other's public value: AI can improve DPI functions through use cases like machine translation and personalized service delivery, while DPI can supply the data foundations for better AI systems. Also catalogs integration challenges, including inference costs, legacy interoperability, bias, and privacy.

publications.title: Leveraging Digital Public Infrastructures for the Common Good in Brazil
publications.summary: Explores how Brazil can design and govern digital public infrastructure according to 'common good' principles to support inclusive and sustainable economic transformation, using Brazil's Rural Environmental Registry (CAR) as a case study. Builds on a partnership between UCL IIPP and Brazil's Ministry of Management and Innovation in Public Services.

publications.title: The Narrow Corridor and the Future of Digital Government
publications.summary: Applies Acemoglu and Robinson's 'narrow corridor' framework to digital government, arguing that new digital state capabilities such as digital identity and digital currencies can create enormous public value but also enable abuse. Proposes a matrix for thinking about futures in which state capacity and society's ability to constrain the state must grow in tandem.

publications.title: Central Banks in a Cashless World
publications.summary: Argues that as cashless transactions rapidly replace physical cash, central banks have an opportunity to serve the public interest by providing or shaping the infrastructure on which digital-payment systems are built — which will require abandoning outdated assumptions about money and re-imagining central banks as market shapers.

publications.title: AI Procurement Checklists: Revisiting Implementation in the Age of AI Governance
publications.summary: Examines how governments regulate public-sector AI procurement, drawing on officials in Brazil, Singapore, and Canada and analyzing the Canadian Directive on Automated Decision-Making and the WEF's AI Procurement in a Box. Identifies three pitfalls — around expertise, risk frameworks, and transparency — that can make AI procurement regulation performative rather than effective.

publications.title: David Eaves on the Promise and Pitfalls of Digital Government
publications.summary: A guest essay surveying the rise of digital government and digital public infrastructure, noting that digitisation is taking on a geopolitical hue as big economies encode their values into digital infrastructure and export it. Calls for more debate over whether new digital state capabilities will expand or limit access to services, opportunity, and democratic values.

publications.title: What is digital public infrastructure?
publications.summary: Defines DPI as society-wide digital capabilities essential to participation in society and markets, and argues public institutions should guarantee DPI is inclusive, foundational, interoperable, and publicly accountable.

publications.title: The Digital Systems Every Country Needs to Succeed in the 21st Century
publications.summary: Argues that the COVID-19 pandemic showed digital identity, payments, and data exchange systems are critical 21st-century infrastructure, and that governments' siloed approach to digital services is wasteful and unsustainable, especially for emerging markets. Calls for an open, well-governed digital public infrastructure model that supports equity, accountability, and country agency.

publications.title: Best Practices for the Governance of Digital Public Goods
publications.summary: Identifies six best practices for governing open-source digital public goods, analyzed through Mark Moore's strategic triangle: public value, legitimacy and support, and operational capability.

publications.title: Funding Digital Government Initiatives
publications.summary: Reports on a closed-door roundtable of major donors in the digital government space, structured around a 2x2 model of funding choices: internal digital teams versus vendors, and multi-sector platforms versus sector-specific projects. Finds funders shifting toward cross-government platforms and internal capacity, while lacking clear strategies.

publications.title: Deploying the Once-Only Policy: A Privacy-Enhancing Guide for Policymakers and Civil Society Actors
publications.summary: A policy brief on the 'once-only' policy, under which citizens and businesses provide their data to government a single time and agencies share and reuse it to deliver better services. Examines how to deploy once-only in a privacy-enhancing way. Authored by Naeha Rashid as part of the digital HKS policy brief series led by Eaves.

publications.title: Teaching Public Service in the Digital Age: Syllabus Lectures
publications.venue: Teaching Public Service in the Digital Age
publications.summary: An open teaching resource offering detailed lesson plans, presentations, and more than 80 video lectures covering the eight-unit Teaching Public Service in the Digital Age syllabus, which David Eaves co-founded. The lectures span digital-era government topics from government as a platform and agile delivery to data, security, and digital transformation strategy.

publications.title: Government as a Platform: How Policy Makers Should Think about the Foundations of Digital Public Infrastructure
publications.summary: Argues that siloed, agency-by-agency digitization has duplicated costs and fragmented government services, and makes the case for a platform model built on shared APIs, open standards, and canonical datasets, drawing on Estonia's X-Road and India's experience. Also flags governance risks, including institutional design, citizen privacy, and the power of agencies that control core platforms.

publications.title: The State of Digital Transformation (report series)
publications.summary: An annual report series capturing insights from the digital services convening that Eaves co-hosted with Public Digital, bringing together leaders of national and subnational digital service teams from over 30 governments. The reports document shared challenges and emerging practice in digital transformation, including funding models, platform governance, talent, and service delivery.

publications.title: Aadhaar: India's Big Experiment with Unique Identification (A & B)
publications.summary: Examines India's biometric ID system: its promise for service delivery and anti-corruption versus surveillance and exclusion risks.

publications.title: Do We Still Need Systems Integrators?
publications.summary: Argues that systems integrators are a symptom of poor systems architecture: modern government IT should be designed from the outset to expose data and functionality through APIs, as Amazon did under Bezos's famous internal mandate. No newly built government system should require a systems integrator.

publications.title: UK Government Digital Service: Moving Beyond a Website
publications.summary: Charts the UK Government Digital Service's evolution from GOV.UK toward platform services, and the institutional battles that followed.

publications.title: After the Collapse: Open Government and the Future of Civil Service
publications.summary: A chapter arguing that governments remain 'analog systems' in structure, values, and culture, and that forces like social media and open source are pushing them toward a platform model. Explores what the Coasean collapse, the long tail of public policy, and gift-economy norms mean for the future of the civil service.
